title: Felix trembles (Acts 24)
hook: a governor hears of justice and self-control and says: another time
tomorrow: a king tells Paul he's almost persuaded. what does Paul wish him?

segments.voice: That was a week of hard roads: a riot calmed, a young man in a window, a goodbye by the sea, a belt, a story on the stairs, and a nephew's warning. Yesterday's line: take heart, Paul.
screen: `TAKE HEART, PAUL.` → `A WEEK OF HARD ROADS.`

segments.voice: The snooze button. The reply you'll send later. The talk you'll have with someone once things calm down. A courtroom in Caesarea: a hired speaker named Tertullus calls Paul "a pestilent fellow," "a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes," and the governor, Felix, puts the case off. Some days later he sends for Paul to hear him again. Acts says Paul spoke of justice, self-control and judgment, and Felix trembled. Then he says: not now.
screen: `THE SNOOZE BUTTON.` → `A PESTILENT FELLOW.` → `FELIX TREMBLES, THEN: NOT NOW.`

segments.voice: First Paul answers the charges calmly. He doesn't hide what he is: "after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers." And he says what he works at: "herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men." Felix comes back with his wife, Drusilla, and hears Paul "concerning the faith in Christ." Then the moment the chapter turns on: "And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee." Righteousness, temperance, judgment: justice, self-control, and an account still to come. Something in Felix shakes. And his answer is an everyday sentence. Not no. Just: later. Acts doesn't make him a villain, and it doesn't flatter him either. He sends for Paul often and talks with him, but Acts adds that he hoped Paul would pay him to be freed. The days stack up. After two years a new governor arrives, and Felix leaves Paul bound. Here's the one to tell a friend: Acts never says the convenient season came.
screen: `CONCERNING THE FAITH IN CHRIST.` · `RIGHTEOUSNESS, TEMPERANCE, JUDGMENT.` · `NOT NO. JUST: LATER.` · `TWO YEARS, AND PAUL STILL BOUND.` · then, large: `A CONVENIENT SEASON.`

segments.voice: Name one thing that matters that you've been putting off: a call, an apology, a visit. The wish: it's done. The obstacle: the quiet voice that says later. The plan: the first small step, and the hour you'll take it. Small is fine; small and soon beats big and someday.
Felix trembles. A governor who heard about justice and self-control, shook, and said: another time.
The line for today: a convenient season, the one Felix waited for and Acts never shows. Two weeks done.

howItsDone: Some Christians read Felix's answer in Acts 24 as a warning against putting off what matters; some preachers quote his words, "a convenient season", when they speak about the present moment.

fork.setup: you've meant to visit your great-aunt in her care home for months. this weekend is free, and a friend invites you to the lake. what fits Felix's story?

go to the lake; a better weekend will come soon.
send a card instead; it's the thought that counts.
fork.reveal: Felix kept waiting for a convenient season, and Acts never shows it arriving. what matters rarely gets more convenient.

chat.meaning: Felix trembled, then said: when I have a convenient season. Acts never records that season. What matters is worth saying now.

Felix.meaning: the Roman governor who heard Paul's case
